THE OPERATING PROBLEM

A fixed schedule misses changing conditions.

The next watering decision depends on soil conditions, weather, crop stage and pump capacity. A calendar alone cannot explain which zone should receive attention first.

01

A recent forecast can change the next day’s demand.

Water demand changes with the weather and crop stage. Each new forecast requires the model to reassess every active zone and compare the recommendation with available pump capacity.

02

Several zones may compete for the same water or pump limit.

The useful output needs the original reference and a clear next action.

03

The operator needs to compare the plan with actual application.

A farm operator checks sensor quality and local conditions before any watering decision. This MVP does not control pumps.

THE PROBLEM WORTH SOLVING

WHY NOW

Use each new reading in the next plan.

Soil readings and weather forecasts become more valuable when they change a dated operating plan. The opportunity is to connect the forecast, the water limit and the operator’s recorded cycle.

Agree the baseline and review the result with the person responsible for the work.

02
